entries.content_osis: <div eID="gen29988" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen29989" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen29990" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen29990" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen29989" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen29991" type="x-p"/> Jeremiah, by the commend of God, goes into the court of the Lord's house; and foretells the destruction of the temple and city, if not prevented by the speedy repentance of the people, <reference osisRef="Jer.26.1-Jer.26.7">Jer 26:1-7</reference>. By this unwelcome prophecy his life was in great danger; although saved by the influence of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, who makes a masterly defense for the prophet, <reference osisRef="Jer.26.8-Jer.26.18">Jer 26:8-18</reference>. Urijah is condemned, but escapes to Egypt; whence he is brought hack by Jehoiakim, and slain, <reference osisRef="Jer.26.20-Jer.26.23">Jer 26:20-23</reference>. Ahikam befriends Jeremiah, <reference osisRef="Jer.26.24">Jer 26:24</reference>. <div eID="gen29991" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29992" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen29992" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen29993" type="x-p"/> In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim - As this prophecy must have been delivered in the first or second year of the reign of Jehoiakim, it is totally out of its place here. Dr. Blayney puts it before chap. 36.; and Dr. Dahler immediately after chap. ix., and before chap. 46.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 20</hi> <div eID="gen30002" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen30003" type="x-p"/> Urijah - who prophesied - The process against Jeremiah is finished at the nineteenth verse; and the case of Urijah is next brought on, for he was also to be tried for his life; but hearing of it he fled to Egypt. He was however condemned in his absence; and the king sent to Egypt, and brought him thence and slew him, and caused him to have an ignominious burial, <reference osisRef="Jer.26.21-Jer.26.23">Jer 26:21-23</reference>.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 24</hi> <div eID="gen30003" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen30004" type="x-p"/> The hand of Ahikam - was with Jeremiah - And it was probably by his influence that Jeremiah did not share the same fate with Urijah. The Ahikam mentioned here was probably the father of Gedaliah, who, after the capture of Jerusalem, was appointed governor of the country by Nebuchadnezzar, <reference osisRef="Jer.40.5">Jer 40:5</reference>. Of the Prophet Urijah, whether he was true or false, we know nothing but what we learn from this place. <div eID="gen30004" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen30005" type="x-p"/> That they should not give him into the hand of the people - Though acquitted in the supreme court, he was not out of danger; there was a popular prejudice against him, and it is likely that Ahikam was obliged to conceal him, that they might not put him to death. The genuine ministers of God have no favor to expect from those who are His enemies.  <chapter eID="Jer.26"/> <div eID="gen30005" type="x-p"/>
